name: Michigan
tagline: Keweenaw copper towns, Lake Superior waterfalls, Leelanau orchards and Woodward Avenue.
intro: Michigan's byways follow the Lake Superior shore of the Upper Peninsula and both coasts of the Lower Peninsula, climb the copper country of the Keweenaw, and run down the old main streets of Detroit, Marshall, Bay City and Monroe. This chapter follows the 22 Pure Michigan Byways listed by the Michigan Department of Transportation, a program created in 1993 as Heritage Routes and renamed in 2014. MDOT's list takes in two national forest byways as well, and several of its historic byways are single city streets only a mile or two long.

members.name: M-1 Woodward Avenue
members.blurb: M-1 runs 27 miles from the Detroit River to Pontiac along an old Native American trail, past the Piquette Avenue plant where Ford built early Model Ts and the suburban strip that fills with classic cars each August.
members.note: Shown on the map as Woodward Avenue (M-1) - Automotive Heritage Trail.

members.name: US-41 Copper Country Trail
members.blurb: US-41 climbs the Keweenaw Peninsula from the Portage Lake Lift Bridge to Copper Harbor through old copper mining towns, with spurs past the Quincy smelting works and up Brockway Mountain for a long look over Lake Superior.

members.name: M-65 River Road
members.blurb: River Road follows the Au Sable for 22 miles through the Huron National Forest, where white pine once floated down to Lake Huron mills, past a bronze monument to three lumbermen and a 300-step stair to Iargo Springs.

members.name: Whitefish Bay National Forest
members.blurb: Lake Shore Drive follows Whitefish Bay west from Bay Mills through Hiawatha National Forest hardwoods and wetlands, past the white tower of Point Iroquois Light and overlooks where freighters pass toward the Soo Locks.

members.name: Black River National Forest
members.blurb: County Road 513 follows a 1904 wagon road from Bessemer to Lake Superior, past the Copper Peak ski-flying hill and, in its last three miles, trailheads to five waterfalls on the Black River.

members.name: M-22 Byway
members.blurb: M-22 rounds the Leelanau Peninsula from Traverse City and follows the Lake Michigan shore 116 miles toward Manistee, by orchards and the Sleeping Bear dunes and past the weathered fish shanties of Leland's Fishtown.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: M-37 Old Mission Peninsula
members.blurb: M-37 runs 18 miles up the Old Mission Peninsula between the two arms of Grand Traverse Bay, through cherry orchards and vineyards to the 1870 Mission Point Lighthouse on the 45th parallel.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: M-119 Tunnel of Trees
members.blurb: M-119 winds 20 miles along the Lake Michigan bluffs from Harbor Springs to Cross Village under a canopy of trees, on a road with no shoulders or centerline, past the 1934 Good Hart General Store.
members.note: Shown on the map as Tunnel of Trees (M-119).

members.name: M-123 Tahquamenon
members.blurb: M-123 runs 63 miles from Newberry to Eckerman by way of Paradise, through old forest to the tannin-brown Upper Tahquamenon Falls, some 200 feet wide, and on to the river's mouth at Whitefish Bay.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: US-2 Top of the Lake
members.blurb: US-2 follows the top of Lake Michigan 92 miles from St. Ignace to Manistique, dipping down to long empty beaches and crossing the Cut River gorge on a truss bridge with stairs that lead down underneath it.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: US-23 Sunrise Coast
members.blurb: US-23 follows the Lake Huron shore 200 miles from the Standish train depot to Mackinaw City, on a highway finished in 1913, past Tawas Point and the Thunder Bay sanctuary that protects more than 200 shipwrecks.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: I-69 Recreational
members.blurb: This 80-mile stretch of I-69 crosses Branch and Calhoun counties from the Indiana line, and its exits lead to more than a hundred fishing lakes and to Coldwater, home of the 1882 Tibbits Opera House.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: M-15 Pathway to Family Fun
members.blurb: M-15 runs 74 miles from Clarkston to Bay City as a quieter alternative to I-75, through farmland and past inland lakes, and on the first Saturday in May it hosts a yard sale stretching to Vassar.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: M-35 Hidden Coast
members.blurb: M-35 follows the Green Bay shore 64 miles from Menominee to Gladstone along much of the old Sault and Green Bay Trail, past a fishing museum in an old fishery house and the 1868 Sand Point Lighthouse at Escanaba.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Chief Noonday
members.blurb: M-179 runs 17 miles east from Bradley toward Hastings under tall hardwoods, through the lakes and glacial kettles of Yankee Springs, on a road named for Noahquageshik, the Odawa leader known as Chief Noonday.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: M-134 North Huron
members.blurb: M-134 follows the north shore of Lake Huron 50 miles from I-75 past the 36 Les Cheneaux Islands and the freighter views at DeTour, then crosses by ferry to end on Drummond Island.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: US-31 West Michigan Pike
members.blurb: US-31 and its business loops follow the old West Michigan Pike 184 miles from New Buffalo to Ludington, by beach towns and the Silver Lake dunes, on what MDOT calls Michigan's first paved road built for tourists.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: US-12 Heritage Trail
members.blurb: Michigan Avenue leaves downtown Detroit on the old Sauk Trail and runs 208 miles to New Buffalo, through the lake-dotted Irish Hills and Coldwater, and over the St. Joseph River beside the 1922 Mottville camelback bridge.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: US-2 Iron County Heritage Trail
members.blurb: This short route links Crystal Falls and Iron River in the iron-mining country of the western Upper Peninsula, from the courthouse atop Crystal Falls to Larson Park, thought to be the first roadside park in the country.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: I-94 Marshall's Territorial Road
members.blurb: A mile of Michigan Avenue through the National Historic Landmark district of Marshall, a town that built a governor's mansion in 1839 hoping to become the capital, with the Polynesian-tinged Honolulu House of 1860 near its fountain circle.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: M-15 and M-25 Center Avenue/Bay City
members.blurb: M-25 follows Center Avenue for a mile and a half through Bay City's lumber-baron neighborhood, where Italianate and Queen Anne mansions from the 1870s onward stand back on broad lawns under old street trees.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: M-125 Monroe Street
members.blurb: Two miles of Monroe Street carry M-125 across the River Raisin past about 40 historic sites, among them the Old Village district and a 14-foot bronze of Custer on horseback, near the War of 1812 battlefield.
members.note: Shown on the map as Monroe Street (M125).
